nodes.label: Meridian Repository Guide
nodes.rationale: Operational map of the autonomous Meteora DLMM agent, its safety boundaries, runtime flow, learning system, and validation workflow.

nodes.label: Centralized Deploy Safety Checks
nodes.rationale: On-chain mutation safety is centralized in the executor so threshold, balance, range, duplicate-position, and single-sided-SOL constraints remain explicit and auditable.

nodes.label: Hybrid Deterministic and LLM Management Cycle
nodes.rationale: Mechanical close and claim rules run deterministically, while the LLM is reserved for natural-language position instructions and other hard cases.
nodes.norm_label: hybrid deterministic and llm management cycle

nodes.label: Walk-forward Rank Lift ML Gate
nodes.rationale: ML blend weight is governed by chronological-fold ranking lift rather than raw classification accuracy because the label base rate makes accuracy misleading.

nodes.label: Dead-man Watchdog
nodes.rationale: A heartbeat written by the daemon lets an external watchdog distinguish a hung process with open positions from an ordinary crash handled by process restart.

nodes.label: Dry-run Before Live Capital
nodes.rationale: Autonomous trading can lose funds, so behavior should be verified in dry-run mode before live deployment and capital should remain bounded.

nodes.label: Once-per-session Mutation Guard
nodes.rationale: Destructive tools such as deploy, swap, and close are locked after use to prevent duplicate financial actions in one ReAct run.

nodes.label: CLI Live Trade Confirmation
nodes.rationale: CLI mutations require dry-run, an explicit confirmation flag, or an allow-list environment switch to reduce accidental live execution.

nodes.label: Threshold Evolution Schema
nodes.rationale: Only explicitly mapped thresholds may evolve, each with section mapping, hard bounds, precision, and a maximum fractional step.

nodes.label: Bounded Structured Decision Memory
nodes.rationale: The log is sanitized and capped at 100 entries so recent deploy, close, skip, and no-deploy reasons can be injected without unbounded prompt growth.

nodes.label: Fail-closed Deployer Blocklist
nodes.rationale: An unreadable safety blocklist throws instead of silently treating all deployers as safe.

nodes.label: Container Heartbeat Healthcheck
nodes.rationale: The healthcheck marks the container unhealthy when positions are open and the management heartbeat is stale; restart policy separately covers crashes.

nodes.label: Container Conservative Defaults
nodes.rationale: A missing container config is initialized with one small position, tight sizing, gas reserve, and trailing profit protection.

nodes.label: Non-blocking Shared Learning
nodes.rationale: Network failures are logged and converted to null so HiveMind availability cannot stop local trading and management cycles.

nodes.label: Busy-flag Concurrency Control
nodes.rationale: Module-level busy flags and trigger cooldowns prevent overlapping cycles and duplicate screening from cron, management, polling, and operator entry points.

nodes.label: Performance Record Quarantine
nodes.rationale: Malformed, unit-mixed, implausible, or duplicate closes are excluded before they can contaminate lessons, threshold evolution, Darwin weights, or ML training.

nodes.label: Censored Exit Evolution Guard
nodes.rationale: Take-profit evolution is disabled while trailing profit exits censor the observed winner distribution, preventing a self-reinforcing collapse toward tiny targets.

nodes.label: Daily Tool Action Audit Trail
nodes.rationale: Tool actions are rendered as concise console lines while full structured results are appended to daily JSONL files for operational auditability.

nodes.label: Fee-to-Volatility Expected-Value Gate
nodes.rationale: Fee revenue must compensate for volatility and adverse selection; candidates below the configured ratio receive a zero score rather than a soft penalty.

nodes.label: Quiet-Hours Position Sizing
nodes.rationale: Observed negative UTC windows size positions down, with a nonzero clamp so deployment validation remains well-defined.

nodes.label: Post-Deploy Adverse-Selection Markouts
nodes.rationale: Net PnL near deploy plus 15 and 60 minutes estimates whether informed flow immediately trades against the LP before fees can compensate.

nodes.label: Screener Quant Risk Contract
nodes.rationale: The screener receives pre-ranked candidates and must either deploy exactly once under code-enforced constraints or issue a concrete no-deploy decision.

nodes.label: Manager Exit and Gas-Efficiency Contract
nodes.rationale: Management is framed as mechanical thesis and exit-rule application with explicit attention to gas churn and mandatory cleanup of non-dust inventory after close.

nodes.label: Power-Law Screening Window Scaling
nodes.rationale: Bursty pool activity scales sublinearly across timeframes; a measured exponent of 0.72 avoids rejecting valid 30-minute pools under naive linear scaling.

nodes.label: Degen Moderate and Safe Risk Presets
nodes.norm_label: degen moderate and safe risk presets

nodes.label: Ephemeral Deploy Attribution Staging
nodes.rationale: Screening signals and ML vectors are held briefly in memory so the eventual deployed position can inherit the exact entry-time context.

nodes.label: Darwinian Signal Weight Learning
nodes.rationale: Signals in the top predictive-lift quartile are boosted and bottom-quartile signals are decayed within bounded weights, conditional on having both wins and losses.

nodes.label: Smart-Wallet Position RPC Cache
nodes.rationale: Wallet positions are cached for five minutes and fetched with concurrency three to reduce rate-limit pressure.

nodes.label: Corroborated PnL Exit Safety
nodes.rationale: Loss exits use fresh derived marks and, on suspicious discrepancies, require even the more optimistic source to breach; profit exits use the lower of reported and derived marks.

nodes.label: Telegram command/control security boundary
nodes.rationale: Inbound control is disabled without a configured chat ID; group chats additionally require an explicit sender allowlist to avoid unauthorized trading commands.

nodes.label: Coalesced live-message updates
nodes.rationale: Tool progress is accumulated into one edited Telegram message with delayed flushes and shared typing state to limit rate pressure and operator spam.

nodes.label: Post-merge conviction floor
nodes.rationale: The diagnostic mirrors screening rejection thresholds after multi-source deduplication so operators can locate the exact stage that starves the LLM candidate set.

nodes.label: Non-live root config shadow
nodes.rationale: The root user-config explicitly warns that the application reads data/user-config.json instead, so tools or playbooks that read the root file can make decisions from stale settings.

nodes.label: ML scoring disabled in local shadow config
nodes.norm_label: ml scoring disabled in local shadow config

nodes.label: Post-close learning loop
nodes.rationale: Every close should feed threshold evolution and, when range efficiency was poor, a durable lesson so later entries adapt to realized outcomes.

nodes.label: Optional liquidity layering decision matrix
nodes.rationale: Layering is permitted only when market data gives a specific directional, volatility, or fee-capture reason; the initial deploy is otherwise complete.

nodes.label: Tight DLMM range outperformance thesis
nodes.rationale: The playbook claims 20-40 bins are generally the efficiency sweet spot and widens ranges only as observed volatility increases.

nodes.label: OHLCV and volume entry timing workflow
nodes.norm_label: ohlcv and volume entry timing workflow

nodes.label: Discord Priority Candidate Path
nodes.rationale: Pending Discord signals bypass ordinary discovery and receive immediate deep research, while failed signals are blacklisted.

nodes.label: New-token Two-sided Spot Rule
nodes.rationale: Tokens no older than 30 minutes favor two-sided Spot because uniform liquidity is safer during price discovery than Bid-Ask concentration.

nodes.label: Persisted Wallet-side Intelligence
nodes.rationale: Refreshing enrichment for open pools makes holder concentration, stale intel, and operator flags available to later screening and ML.

nodes.label: Immutable SHA and Latest Image Tags
nodes.rationale: Each main-branch image is published under both a commit-derived tag for traceability and latest for operational convenience.
nodes.norm_label: immutable sha and latest image tags

nodes.label: Bounded Discord Signal Queue
nodes.rationale: Accepted signals are stored newest-first and truncated to 100 records to bound persistence growth.

nodes.label: Fail-open External Risk Checks
nodes.rationale: RugCheck, deployer lookup, blacklist parse, and fee API failures generally pass with warnings, prioritizing signal availability over fail-closed rejection.

nodes.label: Highest-TVL Pool Resolution
nodes.rationale: When an address is a token rather than a pool, the resolver chooses the matching Meteora DLMM pair with the highest reported liquidity.

nodes.label: Intrinsic Motivation State Machine
nodes.rationale: Outcome, skip, observation, and training events update bounded confidence, boredom, curiosity, risk appetite, and satisfaction values persisted across runs.

nodes.label: Legacy Sparse Feature Reconstruction
nodes.rationale: Closed positions with a stored normalized ML snapshot restore the exact entry vector; legacy records reconstruct a sparse approximation from signal and entry metadata.

nodes.label: Out-of-Sample ML Blend Gate
nodes.rationale: ML begins at ten percent influence and gains weight only when walk-forward rank lift is positive, matching its actual use as a candidate ranker.

nodes.label: Emotion-Free Numeric Trade Score
nodes.rationale: Emotional state is retained as prompt context but deliberately excluded from the numeric blended score to avoid boredom-driven overtrading.

nodes.label: Standardized Interpretable Linear Model
nodes.rationale: A small logistic model fits the low-sample, hand-crafted feature regime; dataset z-scoring prevents fixed universe-wide min-max bounds from collapsing real feature variance.

nodes.label: Chronological Walk-Forward Validation
nodes.rationale: Each fold trains only on earlier closes and validates on later closes, preventing future market-state leakage into past decisions.

nodes.label: Expectancy-Weighted Training Labels
nodes.rationale: A positive label requires clearing a PnL hurdle and gradient weight scales with bounded absolute PnL, so large losses teach more than scratch wins.

nodes.label: Performance Record Validation and Quarantine
nodes.rationale: Quarantine malformed performance records instead of silently trusting or discarding them because all downstream learning depends on label integrity.

nodes.label: Never-Trade Strictness Trap
nodes.rationale: Individually defensible filters can compose into an empty funnel; every proposed filter should report its historical incremental rejection rate before enforcement.

nodes.label: Defer Policy Learning Until Adequate Sample Size
nodes.rationale: Strategy clustering, regret analysis, and threshold tuning are dominated by noise before roughly thirty closed positions.
nodes.norm_label: defer policy learning until adequate sample size

nodes.label: Opt-In ML Activation
nodes.rationale: The experimental ML subsystem stays disabled until enough closed-position data exists to train it meaningfully.

nodes.label: Node 24 Anchor and DLMM Compatibility Patch
nodes.norm_label: node 24 anchor and dlmm compatibility patch

nodes.label: Endpoint-Only Replay Bounds
nodes.rationale: Time-stop interpolation is conservative for accelerating losses while endpoint-only stop-loss savings are optimistic because intratrade recovery paths are invisible.

nodes.label: Open-Position Heartbeat Safety
nodes.rationale: A host-level process alerts when the daemon heartbeat is stale while capital remains exposed, with a cooldown that prevents repeated Telegram spam.

nodes.label: Full Management and Screening Pipeline Diagnostic
nodes.norm_label: full management and screening pipeline diagnostic

nodes.label: Bounded Agent Meridian retry policy
nodes.rationale: Remote requests retry only transient statuses with exponential or Retry-After delays inside both elapsed-time and attempt budgets.

nodes.label: Fail-open indicator availability gate
nodes.rationale: If every indicator request fails, entry and exit logic proceeds using existing non-indicator rules rather than treating upstream unavailability as a market signal.

nodes.label: Route-token noise exclusion
nodes.rationale: SOL and major stable assets are excluded because arbitrage wallets touch them as routing plumbing, making their event counts non-informative as trade signals.

nodes.label: Relay transaction validation sandbox
nodes.rationale: Unsigned relay transactions are inspected, constrained to expected accounts and debit mints, simulated, and rejected for unsafe system transfers before wallet signing and submission.

nodes.label: Post-submit close verification loop
nodes.rationale: A relay close is not recorded locally until repeated fresh position reads confirm that the on-chain position disappeared.

nodes.label: Stale deploy-metric fallback
nodes.rationale: Deploy validation compares fresh detail against the screened snapshot and falls back through DLMM data or the recent candidate snapshot when the single-pool API is clearly stale, while failing closed for unverifiable TVL or volatility.

nodes.label: Public-infrastructure PnL model
nodes.rationale: Current balances and fees come from on-chain DLMM state, cost basis and claims from Meteora history, and USD prices from Jupiter; precomputed live PnL is diagnostic rather than authoritative.

nodes.label: Unpriceable PnL tick safety gate
nodes.rationale: Exit decisions should ignore ticks missing token prices or deposit cost basis so upstream price outages cannot manufacture false stop losses.

nodes.label: Balanced geometric opportunity score
nodes.rationale: Trading, LP activity, fees, and liquidity are combined by geometric mean so no candidate can rank highly from one exceptional but unbalanced metric; explicit risk penalties then reduce the score.

nodes.label: Organic holder-growth signal
nodes.rationale: A rising unique-holder trend is used as harder-to-fake confirmation of real accumulation, sampled only for active shortlisted tokens to control API cost.

nodes.label: Stream-primary RPC-fallback orchestration
nodes.rationale: The tracker normally ingests the low-latency websocket stream and activates Helius polling only while the stream is stale, preventing duplicate continuous ingestion while retaining availability.

nodes.label: Forward-return Signal Feedback
nodes.rationale: Alert prices are snapshotted and evaluated at 15 minutes, 1 hour, and 6 hours so signal weights can be tuned against realized outcomes instead of intuition.

nodes.label: Pump Park and Rearm Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Pumped tokens are parked rather than deleted because market makers may drive a second run after a sufficiently deep retracement.

nodes.label: Outcome-preserving Pruning
nodes.rationale: Tokens with unresolved alerts survive pruning because their future prices are still required for performance measurement.

nodes.label: Layered Token Safety Gate
nodes.rationale: RugCheck is preferred for aggregated authority, liquidity-lock, and concentration risks, with RPC authority and top-holder checks as a fallback.

nodes.label: Arbitrage Flow Leading Indicator
nodes.rationale: Rising touches by arbitrage wallets are treated as early evidence of genuine two-sided flow before lagging aggregate market data fully reacts.

nodes.label: Shared Poller and Stream Event Schema
nodes.rationale: WebSocket arbitrage frames are written into the same tokens and events tables as RPC polling so downstream enrichment, scoring, safety, and alerts remain unchanged.
nodes.norm_label: shared poller and stream event schema

nodes.label: Bounded Stream Observability
nodes.rationale: Only the first five raw frames are logged, followed by minute summaries, preserving protocol visibility without flooding logs.

nodes.label: Safety Before Notification
nodes.rationale: Only a bounded number of highest-ranked candidates receive network safety checks at the alert boundary, controlling cost while vetoing known hazards.

nodes.label: Fresh Runtime Channel Overrides
nodes.rationale: Notification toggles are read from user configuration on every call because the module-level configuration snapshot does not reflect mid-flight operator changes.

nodes.label: Active-token Enrichment Priority
nodes.rationale: The most active tokens are enriched repeatedly so they accumulate enough time-series snapshots for momentum calculations rather than being starved by a constant influx of new tokens.

nodes.label: Interval-flow OBV Proxy
nodes.rationale: OBV uses fresh short-window volume scaled to the enrichment cadence, avoiding repeated counting from overlapping 24-hour volume windows.

nodes.label: Health-aware Endpoint Rotation
nodes.rationale: Endpoints and Helius keys that return rate-limit, authorization, server, or network failures are temporarily penalized and skipped until recovery.

nodes.label: Exponential Jitter Retry Policy
nodes.rationale: Only timeouts, rate limits, and server failures are retried with bounded exponential jitter; ordinary client errors return immediately.

nodes.label: Writable Path Precedence
nodes.rationale: Explicit environment directories take priority, followed by writable deployment volumes and repository-local fallbacks, so persistence works across local and container runtimes.

nodes.label: Advisory Position Trends
nodes.rationale: Snapshot-derived fee and PnL trends advise deterministic close logic but do not independently mutate positions or replace hard exit rules.

nodes.label: CLI Timer Unref Guard
nodes.rationale: Timers are unreferenced in one-shot CLI mode so background cache, heartbeat, and polling intervals cannot keep commands alive after output is produced.
